headline: Peace Hopes Lift Stocks While Chips Slide; Consumer and Housing Lead Mid-Session Charge
body_html:
Equities are broadly higher through Monday's midday session, with advancing issues outpacing decliners by nearly two-to-one across the 519-name universe — 335 names in the green against 182 in the red. The dominant theme is geopolitical relief: reports that President Trump called off a planned strike on Iran to pursue a negotiated settlement have drained risk premium from oil markets and sent a wave of optimism into equities, lifting gold while the dollar softened.

Consumer names lead sector performance, up 1.62%, with Homebuilders close behind at 1.42% and Software adding 1.38%. Healthcare is modestly positive at 0.81%, and Industrials contribute 0.67%. The laggards tell a cleaner story: Semiconductors are the session's worst-performing group, down 2.46%, dragged by broad chip-sector selling. Energy is off 0.73% even as individual oil-services names push higher, and Materials are essentially flat at negative 0.08%.

Supernus Pharmaceuticals stands as the session's standout mover, surging 12.45% on no immediately apparent sector catalyst, suggesting company-specific news is in play. Into the close, traders will watch whether the semiconductor selloff deepens and whether crude's slide stabilises — both will set the tone for Tuesday's open.

briefs.headline: Supernus Rockets to Session-Best Gain on Mystery Catalyst
briefs.body: Supernus Pharmaceuticals is the clear standout of the Monday session, jumping 12.45% and sitting well clear of every other name in the universe. No sector-wide driver is evident in Healthcare-Pharma, which is only modestly positive on the day, pointing to a company-specific development as the likely fuel. Traders will be watching for news flow into the afternoon.

briefs.headline: Chip Stocks Bear the Brunt as Semis Sink 2.46%
briefs.body: Semiconductors are the session's worst-performing sector by a wide margin, off 2.46% as Monday trading unfolds. United Microelectronics is down 7.04% and MaxLinear has shed 6.14%, with semi-equipment name FormFactor falling 4.93%. The broad chip retreat stands in contrast to a constructive tape elsewhere and may reflect rotation away from the group after recent outperformance.

briefs.headline: Oil Retreats as Trump Opts for Diplomacy Over Military Action Against Iran
briefs.body: Crude prices are under pressure after reports emerged that President Trump cancelled a planned military strike on Iran in favor of pursuing a negotiated settlement. The news has also lifted risk appetite in equities broadly, with gold advancing as the U.S. dollar retreated. OPEC's latest output increase is being treated by analysts as a secondary factor for now, though its longer-term supply implications remain in focus.

briefs.headline: Corteva Plunges Nearly 12% to Lead All Decliners
briefs.body: Agricultural-chemicals company Corteva is the session's deepest loser, tumbling 11.90% in a move that stands well outside normal trading ranges. The drop appears company-specific rather than sector-driven, as broader Materials and Agriculture names are not exhibiting comparable weakness. No other name in the universe is close to matching Corteva's intraday loss through midday.

briefs.headline: Boot Barn and Builders FirstSource Reflect Consumer and Housing Strength
briefs.body: Boot Barn, up 5.60%, and Builders FirstSource, gaining 4.81%, are amplifying the leadership signals coming from the Consumer and Homebuilders sectors. The moves suggest spending confidence and residential construction activity remain resilient themes for investors. Both names are among the session's top six gainers, reinforcing the broad-based nature of today's cyclical bid.

briefs.headline: AstraZeneca Slides More Than 7% Against a Constructive Healthcare Tape
briefs.body: AstraZeneca is off 7.08% Monday, a sharp reversal that cuts against the generally positive tone in Healthcare, which is up 0.81% for the session. The divergence implies a stock-specific rather than macro-driven event is weighing on the British pharmaceutical giant's U.S.-listed shares. The move makes AstraZeneca the second-largest decliner across the full universe in today's session.
